answer.evidence: The object is a thin, irregular ivy and leaf decal about 8 rows tall (rows 6-13) and 20 px wide. It is made of light and dark green leaf pixels with no vertical south face, no front-edge line, no eave shadow and no raised body. It lies flat on the ground and is seen from above, which fits the flat kind. With no front face of 3 or more rows, it reads as a top-down slab.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is not a 4x3-tile ground patch. It is a tiny strip of a few green leaves, about 40x10 px, sitting on an empty dark-grey background. It is smaller than one 16x16 tile, so the per-tile facts read 0 and I judged by eye. It has only 4 distinct colours, roughly 3 green steps, against about 5 steps in the grass reference and 7 visible tones in the paving. It has no continuous ground surface, no grass tufts, no soil grain and no per-tile variation. The leaves have no real outline, and the area around them is empty. Next to the references it looks thin, flat and sticker-like, and it does not cover the 4x3 tile area a ground patch needs.
